title: UEFA maintains its World Cups boycott following FIFA crisis
facts: UEFA maintained its threat to boycott FIFA competitions following FIFA's private investment proposals.
UEFA reiterated that it had lost confidence in the leadership of FIFA President Gianni Infantino.
FIFA issued an apology for errors made regarding its plan to sell World Cup stakes through a commercial subsidiary.
UEFA demanded the formal withdrawal of FIFA's plan to sell stakes in major international tournaments.
UEFA demanded binding assurances that FIFA would not attempt private equity sell-offs of competitions in the future.
FIFA convened a high-level leadership summit in Morocco to address the governance crisis.
FIFA announced following the Morocco summit that Gianni Infantino had the full backing of attending senior staff.
UEFA member associations voted to boycott FIFA tournaments if the private investment initiative proceeded.
Gianni Infantino abandoned the project to sell private stakes in the World Cup after widespread backlash.
South American football confederation CONMEBOL welcomed the cancellation of FIFA's private investor project.
CONMEBOL expressed official concern regarding repeated unilateral decisions made by FIFA leadership.
UEFA stated that assertions of support from FIFA-employed staff did not alter its boycott position.
UEFA declared that conditions required to withdraw its boycott threat had not been satisfied by FIFA.
Gianni Infantino faces a challenge to his FIFA presidency following European opposition.
The FIFA private investor plan intended to commercialize tournament revenues through an independent subsidiary entity.
